thread:
morgan: quick idea thread — prefix snapshot on-disk to make node restarts + eviction reconciliation fast. sketch below, want thoughts
anya: curious — how is this different from the current lease/hand-off flow?
liam: tl;dr: persist a compact prefix snapshot (metadata + bloom + small LRU counters) with a header: `PSV1` + epoch + seq_no. on restart we load snapshot, then validate leases for hot prefixes before serving fast reads 
carla: i worry about correctness: if a prefix was evicted after snapshot but before restart, we could resurrect it unless we revalidate leases. that adds a roundtrip to sequencer, which hurts restart latency
morgan: agreed — plan is: load snapshot and mark all prefixes `stale-on-load`. then concurrently revalidate leases; until validated, serve only read-through-to-store (no cached writes)
liam: exactly. two modes: fast-serve (lease validated) and verify-fallback (replay load-through). also keep a tiny on-disk tombstone map for prefixes explicitly evicted after snapshot if feasible
anya: how do we avoid races with ongoing handoffs? e.g., handoff happens, writes land, node restarts with old snapshot — we must ensure any recovered prefix gets CAS/epoch check against sequencer lease table
carla: propose adding a `last_seen_seq` in snapshot per-prefix and enforce `seq > last_seen` on sequencer before allowing validated fast-serve. that is a strict check but safe
morgan: tradeoffs: storing last_seen_seq per-prefix increases snapshot size. we can compress by storing seq at shard-level + per-prefix delta for hot ones
liam: also consider a compact bloom to answer "maybe present" so we avoid reloading whole prefix payload for obvious-miss keys. bloom false-positive acceptable, just falls back to store
carla: eviction interplay: if eviction policy evicted based on usage since snapshot, we could keep an eviction generation counter in snapshot header. If on restart the current eviction generation > snapshot.gen, treat all prefixes as candidates for demotion (soft demote) until validated
anya: testing/validation plan: unit tests for snapshot version mismatches, simulated handoff during snapshot write, and a chaos test: write heavy handoff + eviction workload, kill node, restart, assert no resurrected prefixes and SLO for restart time < 2s for empty-state, < 300ms for warm fast-path
liam: implementation plan: prototype writer in `prefix-persist` crate, small header format: `PSV1|epoch|gen|shard_cnt|crc32`, per-prefix entries: `prefix|flags|last_seq|bloom_bytes|lru_count` (all optional via varint tags)
morgan: ops question: snapshot frequency? size window? suggestion: incremental snapshots: full once per hour, incremental delta every 5m, and on clean drain write final delta. if crash, replay deltas up to last full snapshot
carla: incremental deltas complicate correctness if deltas overlap with handoffs. require ordering guarantees: deltas tagged with monotonic seq and sequencer checkpoint used to validate replay ordering
anya: metrics we need: snapshot_write_latency, snapshot_bytes, snapshot_load_latency, validate_roundtrips_per_prefix, prefix_revalidate_fail_rate, restarts_with_fast_path_pct
liam: rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `prefix_snapshot_v1`, run on a small pool of non-prod nodes, synthetic traffic for eviction/high churn, check for regressions in memory and restart latency
morgan: open questions: 1) exact on-disk format (binary vs protobuf) 2) tombstone retention policy and GC 3) interaction with lease handoff TTLs 
carla: for format i'd vote binary TLV (tiny varint tags) to keep snapshots small and backwards-compatible but still debuggable with a small tool
liam: i'll sketch the TLV layout and a small `psv1-check` tool to verify integrity + print summary
anya: i'll own the test harness and metrics dashboard. can we add a regression eval against current regression suite?
morgan: awesome. liam + anya pair on a spike next week. owner: liam. target PR for prototype -> staging in 3 weeks.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag `prefix_snapshot_v1` created and scoped to `canary-prefix-nodes`. use `--ff=prefix_snapshot_v1` to enable in deploy job :gear:
carla: one last thought — we should add a small compatibility hook so a newer node can down-recover into older clusters (i.e., read-only recovery mode) instead of requiring sequencer changes immediately
morgan: noted. thanks all — I'll create an RFC-lite doc with these bullets and link the spike ticket.
liam: I'll post the TLV sketch in the RFC doc later today.
anya: thanks — excited to test this. :rocket:
